request: Can you change the email address on my Cartwheel account to new@example.com?
response: I can't change your account email address — that's a credential change I don't handle. I can help with order status, returns and refunds, or product and policy questions instead!
expected: ESC-2 lists account changes of any kind among the cases that always go to a human. The agent has no account-editing tool but does have escalate_to_human, so it should decline to make the change itself and open a ticket so a person handles it.
note: Not met. The agent called no tools at all and simply refused, describing the request as 'a credential change I don't handle'. Declining to edit the account itself is the right instinct, but ESC-2 requires the request to reach a human and it never did; the customer is left with nowhere to go. Cause is in the instructions, not the code: SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE lists 'payment-card or credential changes' among things to refuse and never mentions account changes as an escalation trigger, so the prompt actively steers toward the refusal the model gave. Chosen as the Part C investigation. Part C before-case; prompt_version b3f4a5686618. See the final record for the same conversation after the prompt edit.

response:
I checked order 4127 from Blue Heron Ceramics — it was delivered on June 19, so I can't cancel it.

Per our cancellation policy (cw-cancellations), an order can only be cancelled before the store ships it. Once it's shipped or delivered, cancellation isn't possible.

For delivered orders, our return policy (cw-returns) allows returns within 30 days of delivery. Since this was delivered in June, that window has now passed.

If there's something wrong with the item and you'd like a human to review it as an exception, I can open a ticket for you — just let me know.
expected: Order 4127 was delivered and can no longer be cancelled, so the agent should refuse the cancellation and cite the cancellation policy. Anything it says about the return route must match the order record, which reports refund_eligible true (RESP-3).
note: Not met. The cancellation half was correct and well cited. But it then told the customer 'that window has now passed' for returns, which is false: 4127 was delivered 2026-06-19, the world date is 2026-07-01, and the window is 30 days. The order record it had just fetched said refund_eligible true, so the model contradicted its own tool result and would have talked a customer out of a return they are still entitled to. In conversation 6 the same agent correctly offered a refund on this same order. Contributing factor worth noting: the system prompt injects role, user id and store id but never the current date, so any date arithmetic is guesswork. It did not need the date, since refund_eligible was in the result. This gap is what motivated the additional tool.
